full_judgment:
19. In the case of Durgabati Banerjee and others vs Taharulla Mia reported in 44 CWN 849, in the background of the reported case noticed by the learned Judges relating to the general question of the grounds upon which a person is entitled to have a decree against him set aside on the ground that it had been fraudulently obtained it has been held : "that a plaintiff is not entitled to have a decree against him set aside on the ground that it had been fraudulently obtained merely by reason of the fact that the claim in the original suit was false or without any cause of action or merely because the decree was obtained by false representation or suppression of facts, provided the person so applying for a reversal of the decree in the original suit was not prevented by the fraud of the decree-holder from placing his case before the Court". It may be mentioned in the instant case proposition of law laid down in the case of Mahomed Golab was accepted as the correct proposition of law and disapproved-the decision taking view different from the proposition of law in Mahomed Golab's case. 

 20. In the case of Nemchand Tantia vs Kishinchand Chellaram (India) Ltd. reported in AIR 1959, Calcutta, 776 and in the case of Atul Chandra Sarkar vs East Bengal Commercial Bank Ltd and another reported in AIR 1960, Calcutta, 309 the proposition of law laid down in Mahomed Golab's case considered to be the correct proposition of law regarding the scope of the suit seeking setting aside of the ex parte decree on the ground of fraud. In the case of Azizur Rahman vs Sudhangshu Kumar Mitra and another reported in 4 DLR 636 scope of the suit filed seeking setting aside of the ex parte decree on the ground of fraud was considered and it was held: "It is now well settled that an ex parte decree can be set aside by a new action when the Court passing it had been misled by fraud" and that an ex parte decree in a later action can be set aside when the same was obtained by suppression of summons. In the case of Ananta Kumar Bepari vs Jamini Mohan Das and others reported in 4 DLR 487 it has been observed that an ex parte decree cannot be set aside merely on the ground of perjured evidence and false claim unless in obtaining the decree fraud is established to have been practiced. In the case of Chapala Sundari Devi vs Wahed Ali and others reported in 11 DLR 376 it has been observed "The principle of law is now well established that an ex parte decree cannot be re-opened in a later action brought to set it aside on the ground of fraud, simply because the claim decreed ex parte was false. The mere fact that the claim was false or without any cause of action will not entitle a defendant to set aside the decree obtained in the suit. The only ground on which the reversal of the ex parte decree in the previous suit can be successfully prayed for in a suit for setting aside that decree is that the plaintiff was prevented by the fraud of the decree-holder in the previous suit from placing his case before the Court. In other words, he will have to prove that the notice of the previous suit was not served on him, and this non-service was due to the fraud of the plaintiff in the previous suit".
